purpose: Internal benchmark: OceanLens underwater image enhancement on two BMCAM_001 reef images (compare against sea-thru bench).

model.name: OceanLens
model.license: MIT (repo LICENSE, AIRLabIISc 2024). No non-MIT third-party weights used: the run trains the two small CNNs from scratch per batch; the repo's bundled sample checkpoints (Model Checkpoints (Sample)/) were NOT used.
model.how_it_runs: Sea-thru-style self-supervised per-batch optimization (Ocean_Lens/train.py). No pretrained enhancement weights required; BackscatterNet + DeattenuateNet are optimized on the input batch itself (adaptive backscatter loss + deattenuation losses), then the corrected image is saved.

inputs.image_size_px: 1000x562 (processed at native size; --height 562 --width 1000, so the model's Resize is an identity)
inputs.preprocessing: None. Note: the OceanLens paper optionally pre-applies gray-world white balance and gamma correction; this run fed the raw JPEGs (no WB/gamma) to keep the benchmark comparable to the sea-thru run.

depth.note: Paper used Depth-Anything-V2-Large / Monodepth2; Small used here per bench setup (already in HF cache). Pipeline output (brighter = nearer) was normalized to 0-255 and INVERTED (255 - v) so larger = farther, then saved as 8-bit grayscale PNG, matching how OceanLens's data loader consumes depth (relative units, not metres; --depth_16u not set).

invocation.python: scratchpad/seathru_bench/venv/bin/python (torch 2.13.0 CPU, torchvision 0.28.0, kornia/pandas/openpyxl/tensorboard added for this run)
invocation.iterations: 500 per network (both images in one batch of 2); --seed 1337 passed but train.py never uses it, so weight init is unseeded (results vary slightly run to run)
invocation.device: CPU (repo code only checks CUDA; MPS not used)

model_reported_metrics.note: From train.py's built-in evaluation (on 256x256-resized outputs for UIQM); full xlsx + intermediates (direct/backscatter/attenuation maps, checkpoint) in scratchpad oceanlens_bench/output/

deviations_and_caveats: Repo's Ocean_Lens/inference.py is a tkinter GUI and needs a trained checkpoint; the README's custom-input path is train.py (per-batch self-optimization), which is what was run.
Depth-Anything-V2-Small instead of the paper's Large/Monodepth2 depth sources.
Depth maps are relative 8-bit (0-255) with a hand-chosen inversion convention, not metric depth.
No WB/gamma preprocessing applied (paper sometimes pre-applies both).
Optimization is per-batch and unseeded in practice, so exact pixel values are not reproducible run to run.
Inputs are the 1000x562 transmitted JPEGs, not native captures.
